'''''Sporobolus alopecuroides''''' is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] known by the common name '''foxtail pricklegrass'''. It is native to Europe, the Middle East, and North Africa. It is also known in the western United States as a common and widespread [[introduced species]], especially in sandy areas around water, such as lakesides. It has also been collected at shipping points near [[Philadelphia]] but has not been seen there in about a century.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110611150938/http://herbarium.usu.edu/webmanual/info2.asp?name=Crypsis_alopecuroides&type=treatment Grass Manual Treatment]</ref> This is an annual grass producing mostly upright and unbranching stems, often dark in color, up to about 75 centimeters in maximum height. The green leaves are up to 12 centimeters long, sometimes waxy in texture. The [[inflorescence]] is a dense cylindrical [[panicle]] of tiny green to purple spikelets.
